source.title: Understanding Edge-of-Stability Training Dynamics with a Minimalist Example
source.authors: Xingyu Zhu; Zixuan Wang; Xiang Wang; Mo Zhou; Rong Ge

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including supplementary materials; no apparent cutoff affecting the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training loss and convergence on a small CIFAR-10 binary subset using full-batch gradient descent and squared loss. This bears conceptually on whether gradient training reaches low training error, but it does not reproduce the classification-error benchmarks and recipes in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper's CIFAR-10 subset results and stated convergence outcomes bear on V1. Most of the paper's scalar-network sharpness analyses, and its discussion of prior work on learning rates, initialization and batch normalization, do not directly test another listed version. The 50-sample CIFAR-10 task uses binary labels and mean squared loss, not training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5's edge-of-stability component through full-batch neural-network experiments and a minimalist model with convergence proofs. The record misses these results and incorrectly links fully connected regression experiments to V1's convolutional classification claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors emphasize sharpness adaptivity and concentration, prove local convergence near the stability threshold for a degree-4 scalar model, contrast its dynamics with degree-2 models, and show similar parabolic convergence in deep fully connected networks on a small CIFAR-10 subset. Their analysis does not establish global convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The real-data experiment uses an over-parameterized fully connected network on a 50-sample binary CIFAR-10 subset with mean squared loss, rather than a standard CIFAR classification benchmark and classification-error measure. The paper also studies scalar product objectives and rank-1 matrix factorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation (ELU or tanh) and batch size affect reported converging sharpness; the paper states small-batch SGD has significantly lower sharpness than large-batch SGD. All mini-batch runs are reported to have loss below 10−8.

fits_no_version.finding: The fully connected ELU and tanh models fit the 50-image binary CIFAR-10 subset, with all Figure 29 runs reaching squared loss below 10^-8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These fully connected networks can interpolate this small binary dataset under the tested GD and SGD recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Small-batch SGD reaches substantially lower final sharpness than full-batch training while still attaining loss below 10^-8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final sharpness depends on batch size in these interpolating networks; V5's full-batch condition does not cover small-batch SGD.

record.problems: The real-world CIFAR-10 experiment uses only 50 examples from two classes and mean squared loss, so it does not directly establish near-zero classification error on the standard benchmark. No explicit control comparison for the CIFAR-10 loss result is reported. The minibatch loss result is aggregated across batch sizes and initializations rather than reported separately for each condition.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks reaching near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels and the stated recipe comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient preservation, and comparative training speed or trainable depth.

The complete wide-network catapult sequence relative to initial linearized stability, its larger-rate divergence boundary, and divergence from initially subthreshold neural-network runs are not systematically tested.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Sharpness trajectories for the existing CIFAR-10 full-batch rows: threshold oscillation during declining loss, ELU final sharpness 199.97 versus threshold 200, and qualitatively similar tanh behavior.

Synthetic-network comparison: five-layer width-50 ReLU network tracks thresholds 200, 300, and 400; two-layer width-10 linear network with initialization rescaling (4, 0.1) converges distinctly below thresholds 30, 35, and 40.
Degree-4 scalar convergence and threshold concentration, including the restricted initialization region and step-size assumptions; contrasting degree-2 convergence substantially below threshold.

Separate batch-size-50 results for ELU and tanh at η = 0.005, 0.01, and 0.02: final sharpness close to corresponding thresholds 400, 200, and 100, with loss below 10^-8 across ten initializations per condition.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. Squared loss is appropriate evidence for V5 when paired with sharpness measurements. The exclusion from V1 rests principally on the fully connected architecture, not merely on the use of squared loss.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a binary 50-sample CIFAR-10 subset with mean squared loss and full-batch gradient descent. Does not report CIFAR-100, standard CIFAR-10 classification error, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam, smaller-model comparisons, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
